summary.intent: Work through the callisto repo's NEXT-WORK plan (v1 hardening): ship parallel lanes of fixes, refactors, test debt, docs cleanup and CI hygiene as separate PRs, keeping the plan as local-only tracking and moving forward autonomously.
summary.outcome: Opened many PRs with local `just ci` passing: #202 SYS-RETRY fix, #203 mixed-routing test, #204 docs refresh, stack #207 (#205 init tests move, #206 templates, #208 SYS-NAPI), R3 derive split, #271 CI hygiene, #272 E317, plus pre-mode no-repeat-bump/E318, range hard-stop/E319, dist-tag/snapshot refusal, dead-code deletion, status warning/failed-command tail, canonical ids with schemaVersion 2, and the final CLI `--package` qualification change being committed. Closed PR #201 after the user said the plan should not be in a PR. Several items remain deferred or awaiting user decisions.

repo: Plan/tracking docs live at `.claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md`, excluded via `.git/info/exclude`; they must never be committed or put in a PR.

Work is done in per-task git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`, one PR each, with `just ci` run one at a time. The wrapper's 'exit code 0' is not trustworthy; the log's own `exit=` line is the real result (e.g. fmt-check failures showed `exit=1`).
Signed commits are required, and per AGENTS.md no session link goes in commits or PRs.
Native stacks of PRs are linked with `gh stack` (e.g. stack #207 holds #205, #206, #208).

Callisto publishes four crates (callisto-model MIT, manifests, graph, cli under FSL), plus dev-only callisto-fixtures. They are one fixed group in callisto.toml and move in lockstep. The v1 plan is all four to 1.0 together, libraries marked internal with no API guarantee.
Package references in config and CLI args now require the qualified `eco/name` form (E317); bare names are rejected. Changeset entries and pre.json keys keep native names.
Reports use canonical `ecosystem/name` keys with schemaVersion 2.
Docs and specs (docs/specs/*.json, docs/errors.md, architecture notes) must be updated alongside behavior changes; the error table is numbered (E317, E318, E319 added).
The release e2e harness fakes gh, cargo and registry, so fixes touching those are not proven against the real tools. The SYS-NAPI test used the real binary and real jq instead.
On macOS, bash lacks `mapfile` and sed differs from GNU, so generated workflow scripts and edits need portable forms.

code.finding: Local tag observation errored on multi-paragraph/signed tag messages; fixed to read only the object type, since annotation text is never compared per the spec.

The napi roster is now derived per intent package via `callisto matrix`, and placement reads the plan job's `napi_dirs` output. The intent omits `artifactSlots` when empty, so jq `.artifactSlots[]` iterated null.
R3 split the large derive function into stage functions, with `uploads_by_package` moved into OpIndex, guarded by characterization snapshots committed first and a mutation check.

Selection now treats a package whose current version is tagged on HEAD as resumable, observing registry, tag and GitHub release before deciding. A tag on an older commit settles without contacting providers.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first, then prove new tests catch regressions with deliberate mutations.
For pure moves and refactors, commit snapshots or characterization tests first, then the move, and confirm snapshots pass unchanged.
Scripted bulk edits can silently alter unrelated lines (a fixup script changed two comments); review the staged diff before committing.
Sandbox rejects inline env commands, heredocs, and scripts mentioning git, and only allows edits inside the current worktree, so use script files and Write/Edit tools.
Use an independent review agent for risky changes; its review of #202 found real defects (signed-tag handling, a high-severity dependent-tagged case).
Background CI runs should be checked via their log's exit line, using Monitor while working in other worktrees.

friction: Initially treated NEXT-WORK.md as something to commit and opened PR #201 for it, which the user rejected; it had to be closed and moved to a local excluded file.
Sandbox restrictions (inline env, heredocs, git in scripts, edits outside the worktree) forced many workarounds and worktree switching.
Background sessions couldn't edit the shared checkout, so the plan file status couldn't be updated at one point.
The wrapper reported exit code 0 while CI had actually failed (fmt-check), so the log had to be read each time.
Rebase conflicts in docs/errors.md recurred as parallel PRs each added error codes.
Scripted test-fixture conversions double-prefixed names and corrupted colon-form inputs, requiring fixup scripts.
Initial plan path in the lane summary was wrong, and the michi versioning recommendation was overturned by the user's newer lockstep decision.
open_items: Delete stale branches (docs/next-work-plan, docs/spec-rewrite, fix/native-resolution, docs/crate-consolidation-plan, about 35 local branches): needs the user's per-branch call.
W1 real-service credential check: needs a decision on where it runs in CI.
SYS-MATURIN and W9 (SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION, resolver divergence) remain blocked on D01 and on W2/R1.
W10 needs decisions on distinct target declaration graph edges (RewriteKey) and Python dev group cascade; W11 needs credentials and an approved run.
#204 still lists SYS-RETRY/T08-RETRY, so a follow-up edit is needed after #202 merges.
#202 has no independent review applied to merge-ready state beyond fixes; real gh/cargo/registry reads remain unproven.
cargo-semver-checks deferred until the promised surfaces (CLI schema output, config and report formats) are defined; OIDC trusted publishing is a post-1.0 item.
Possible merge of callisto-manifests into callisto-graph is deferred until after 1.0.

Remaining plan lanes not yet started or finished: R1 walk.rs::build (Lane F), SYS-BARRIER, SYS-PYFILES/SYS-PYROUTES, and removing the never-emitted BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems variant at the wire change.
The final CLI `--package` qualification PR was being committed and rebased; its push and PR opening were not shown.
